tweets.text:
There’s a puzzling eagerness among many AI leaders and experts to increasingly frame artificial intelligence as a zero sum race between U.S. & China. The logic seems straightforward: achieve AGI first, secure geopolitical dominance. But the idea of rushing to create our own version of Dr. Manhattan, maybe just months ahead of a rival nation feels extraordinarily misguided, dangerous, even.

Thomas Friedman's recent column (🎁🔗 in comments) crystalizes my discomfort. AGI is not simply another tech race; it's an existential threshold that demands international cooperation rather than competitive brinkmanship. I am very pessimistic that there is a path were this occurs but  collaboration on creating frameworks for safe and trustworthy AI is far preferable to the destabilizing arms race we seem intent on pursuing. The stakes are too high, and the consequences of failure too severe, for anything less than united action.
